cutoff_window.rule: Include only public web sources published or visibly updated within the last 2 days relative to the run time. Exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, boundary-only, stale, or previously captured items.

qualifying_findings.source_title: 'Ghostcommit' hides prompt injection in images to fool AI agents, steal secrets
qualifying_findings.summary: BleepingComputer reported on a proof of concept pull request that hides malicious instructions in a PNG so a code reviewer misses them, while a later coding agent reads the image and writes repository secrets into source.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: AI code review and coding-agent workflows need multimodal prompt-injection checks, explicit image and binary review rules, secret access isolation, and tests that cover downstream agent behavior after human review.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep exploit/entity background upstream if covered; retain the downstream practice implication for prompt-injection review gates and secret isolation.

qualifying_findings.source_title: The Verification Gap: Why Faster Code Generation Is Making Software Quality Worse
qualifying_findings.summary: Tabnine argued that AI coding assistants have reduced the cost of code generation while leaving validation, testing, maintainability, and architectural judgment as the constrained parts of delivery.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Local verification guidance should frame AI-assisted development around verification capacity, regression ownership, and maintainability review instead of measuring only generated-code throughput.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Route vendor/product background upstream; keep the local practice lens on verification tax and quality gates.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Why AI Agent Governance Can't Be an Afterthought
qualifying_findings.summary: Workato described agent governance as the combined organizational and technical controls needed to deploy, monitor, manage, secure, and cost-control agent fleets before sprawl becomes unmanageable.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Adoption guidance should make governance an upfront rollout requirement with ownership, fleet inventory, policy enforcement, monitoring, and cost controls, not a cleanup phase after pilots spread.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep broad vendor background upstream; retain the downstream practice implication for early governance and operating agreements.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Best MCP Gateway for Claude Code Enterprise Teams 2026
qualifying_findings.summary: TrueFoundry compared MCP gateway approaches for Claude Code rollouts and emphasized centralized MCP server registration, enforceable access policies, audit logs, enterprise identity, and deployment control as enterprise criteria.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: MCP governance pages should distinguish local configuration convenience from enforceable gateway policy and should track tool-call logs by user, server, action, and timestamp.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Entity and product comparison belongs upstream; keep the local practice criteria for governed MCP access.

qualifying_findings.source_title: GPT-5.6 Raises the Bar for Code Review, but Trust and Governance Remain the Real Test
qualifying_findings.summary: Futurum covered Qodo's GPT-5.6 integration for code review and governance workflows, framing model improvements as useful only when embedded in structured quality and productivity workflows.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: AI code review guidance should treat model selection as one component of a review system with trust, governance, measurable productivity, and reliability controls.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep vendor and model coverage upstream; retain downstream practice implications for review governance.

qualifying_findings.source_title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic AI: What Enterprise Security Teams Need to Test
qualifying_findings.summary: Airia argued that enterprise security teams should operationalize OWASP agentic AI risks as systematic testing campaigns, especially prompt injection, excessive agency, and improper output handling.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Security evaluation guidance should map agentic risks to repeatable tests, coverage tracking, and accountability across each deployed agent rather than relying on awareness-only policies.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Route framework and vendor background upstream; retain testing-baseline practice for local verification and governance pages.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Best AI Agent Authentication and Authorization Platforms for Enterprise in 2026
qualifying_findings.summary: Arcade framed enterprise agent authentication around where authorization is enforced, emphasizing agent identities, OAuth/OIDC foundations, token management, and task/resource-aware checks.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Tool-call and MCP guidance should model agent identity separately from user identity and specify where user-agent-task authorization is enforced before tool execution.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep platform comparison upstream; retain the local practice criteria for authorization enforcement boundaries.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Monitoring AI Applications in 2026: What You Actually Need
qualifying_findings.summary: Scout Monitoring described production AI application monitoring as requiring both LLM observability for output quality and token cost and traditional APM for the code path, latency, logs, traces, and errors.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Application-harness guidance should separate model-output observability from application-runtime observability and connect agent-assisted repair to traces that distinguish retrieval, prompt, model, and application defects.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep product background upstream; retain local practice implication for runtime evidence collection and repair loops.

qualifying_findings.source_title: SpaceXAI's Grok 4.5 Undercuts Anthropic and OpenAI on Coding Agent Pricing
qualifying_findings.summary: DevOps.com reported on coding-agent model pricing and token-efficiency claims, while noting a benchmark transparency caveat involving CursorBench training data exposure.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Agent-cost telemetry should track cost per verified outcome, not list price alone, and model benchmark claims need provenance and contamination checks before adoption decisions.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Model/product coverage belongs upstream; keep downstream implications for cost telemetry and benchmark hygiene.

qualifying_findings.source_title: OpenAI ChatGPT Work Ships Files, Not Just Chat. The Enterprise Race Is On
qualifying_findings.summary: Futurum analyzed ChatGPT Work as an artifact-producing agent that combines Codex, connector access, local files, browser context, and approval pauses to create spreadsheets, slides, documents, and web apps.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Application-pattern and governance pages should address finished-artifact review, connector scoping, local-file access, auditability, and approval boundaries when agents move from chat answers to delivered files.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep product and model launch details upstream; retain downstream practice implications for artifact review and connector governance.

qualifying_findings.source_title: The Most Important Developer Tasks in the Agentic AI Era
qualifying_findings.summary: Lushbinary argued that as agents draft more code, developer leverage moves toward code review, system design, precise specification, evaluation, security, orchestration, and debugging work the developer did not personally write.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Adoption guidance should train teams for review depth, specification quality, evaluation habits, and orchestration accountability rather than only prompt syntax or tool familiarity.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Treat broad technique background as upstream-owned; keep the local operating-model implications for developer skill shifts.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Shadow AI Detection: How to Identify Unauthorized AI, Assess Risk, and Build Governance That Protects the Organization
qualifying_findings.summary: Adaptive Security described shadow AI detection as a continuous governance problem requiring visibility into unauthorized AI usage and risk, not a one-time inventory or blanket ban.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Governance pages should include sanctioned-tool inventories, acceptable-use policy, monitoring, training, and risk-based response paths for developers using unapproved AI coding or review tools.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep vendor/background coverage upstream; retain downstream implications for team AI-tool governance and privacy controls.
